title: Why Do Dogs Bury Their Toys and Bones?

Your couch cushions aren't safe, and neither is your yard — here's why.

script: If your dog has ever shoved a bone under your couch cushions or dug a hole in the yard for a half-chewed toy, they're following an instinct that's thousands of years old. Wild canine ancestors didn't have guaranteed meals every day, so when food was abundant, they'd cache the extra for later, burying it to hide it from other animals and to keep it protected until they needed it. Your dog doesn't need to worry about where their next meal is coming from, but that survival wiring never fully disappeared. Burying also has a scent component. Dirt and fabric help mask the smell of a valuable item, which in the wild meant fewer competitors sniffing it out. Some dogs even do a version of this indoors, pushing toys under blankets or pillows using their nose, essentially recreating digging behavior without actual dirt. It's not random destruction, it's resourcefulness. Your dog is quite literally saving something for later, exactly the way their ancestors did for survival. If instincts like this are turning into full-blown destructive habits at your place, the training program linked below can help you redirect that energy productively.
